Work in /opt/nxeon. Fix BLOCK-STORAGE VOLUMES in a live VPS hosting platform. Read `docs/AUDIT-24H.md` (do not edit it).

YOU OWN EXACTLY: `lib/actions-volumes.ts`, `worker/volumes.ts`, `components/customer/Volumes.tsx`. Nothing else — 7 agents work concurrently. `prisma/schema.prisma` is FROZEN.

SCHEMA ALREADY ADDED FOR YOU: `Volume.inUse` (Boolean, default false), `Volume.mountPath` (String?), `Volume.fsType` (String?). Use them.

THE PROBLEMS (all verified):

**1. The UI tells a lie that can destroy data.** `components/customer/Volumes.tsx:172` says *"Data is preserved."* on detach. `lib/actions-volumes.ts:147-164` has NO dependency check and `worker/volumes.ts:236` detaches unconditionally. For the Docker-on-volume layout the migration engine can create, detaching pulls the filesystem out from under running services. Build **safe-detach**: refuse to detach a volume the server depends on (`inUse`), explain exactly what depends on it, and require an explicit informed override rather than a silent one. Fix the copy so it states what actually happens.

**2. Volumes are advertised as portable but are pinned forever.** `lib/actions-volumes.ts:129-131` refuses attaching to any server other than `volume.serverId`, and detach never clears it (`worker/volumes.ts:240`). So a volume is welded to the first server it ever touched. Make them genuinely movable: a DETACHED volume must be attachable to any server the same customer owns. Clear `serverId` on detach. Keep the guard that a volume can only ever attach to ONE server at a time, and only to a server owned by the same customer.

**3. Nothing ever formats or mounts a volume.** There is no `mkfs`/fstab logic in `worker/volumes.ts`; the attach notice at `:204` just tells the customer to do it themselves — for a product sold as "storage upgrade" that is a bad experience and the main reason `inUse` was never knowable. On attach, detect whether the disk already has a filesystem; if blank, format it (ext4) and mount it at a stable path; if it already has one, mount it without touching the data. Record `fsType` and `mountPath`, and add an fstab entry (use UUID, plus `nofail` so a missing volume can never block boot — a server that won't boot because a volume was detached is a far worse failure than an unmounted disk). Set `inUse` accordingly.
**NEVER format a disk that already contains a filesystem or partition table.** Detect first, and if detection is at all ambiguous, refuse and report rather than risk destroying customer data. This is the single most dangerous operation in your scope.

**4. Reinstall protection already exists** (`worker/index.ts:428-448`, `lib/actions.ts:464-471`) — those files are NOT yours; do not touch them. Just make sure your changes stay consistent with that behaviour.

REQUIREMENTS
- Customer data is at stake. Prefer refusing an operation over performing a destructive one on ambiguous evidence.
- The worker talks to Proxmox and over SSH to guests — follow the patterns already in `worker/volumes.ts`. Note that Proxmox config writes are ASYNCHRONOUS: an immediate GET can return the pre-write view, and this file already contains a poll-until-visible loop for exactly that reason. Reuse it; don't reintroduce the race.
- Match the Nxeon dark theme; reuse existing classes. No new visual styles.
- Comment style: explain WHY and cite the real failure prevented.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Do NOT run `npm run build`/`npm run dev`, do NOT restart any systemd service.
- Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"`.
- Do NOT git commit/push, do NOT edit prisma/schema.prisma.
- Do NOT run any real Proxmox mutation, vzdump, mkfs, or SSH command against a live VM. Write the code; do not execute it.

Report: the safe-detach rule, how portability now works, your format-detection logic and why it cannot destroy data, and the fstab strategy.

If the webhook wins the race (Stripe fires it independently of the browser redirect), the customer's
card is charged, the wallet is credited, and the deploy / resize / disk expansion **never happens**.
The redirect lands on a bare server list with no error. `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is populated, so this
is live. The in-code comments assert the opposite ("provisioning runs exactly once even if the
confirm URL is reloaded") — true for reloads, false for webhook-first ordering.

### 4. Three customer-facing promises the code does not keep

| Promise shown to the customer | Reality |
|---|---|
| `CouponField.tsx:60-66` — "Code applied — 20% bonus · Bonus is credited when you add funds" | The cookie is read only by the demo gateway (`lib/actions.ts:527`), which refuses in production. `app/api/stripe/checkout/route.ts` applies no discount. No bonus, no error |
| `Volumes.tsx:172` — "Detach … Data is preserved." | No unmount, no in-use check (`worker/volumes.ts:236`). For a volume holding `/var/lib/docker` — which is exactly what the migration engine puts there — this destroys the server's Docker state |
| `MailSettings.tsx:234` — display name "Shown as the sender name on messages you send" | `lib/actions-mail.ts:431` sends `from: cred.address` with no display name and no `Reply-To`. The field is saved and never used |

Add the **"Daily backups" add-on** (`DeployWizard.tsx:209` → `lib/order.ts:183` → read by nothing),
and the WHOIS-privacy checklist item that ticks green off a DB flag no registrar ever saw
(`lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-151` vs `app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:115`).

### 5. A customer's backup button can delete the platform's backups

`lib/proxmox.ts:413-429` prunes by `vmid` across the whole `backup` PVE storage — which resolves to
`/tank/backup`, the same directory `scripts/backup-vms.sh:31-35` writes host-level platform backups
into. A customer clicking "Create backup" prunes *all* archives for that VMID down to 2, platform
copies included. Currently masked because the production drop-in also forces `keep-last=2`, but the
two retention policies are meant to differ (the user asked for system=3, customer=2) and the moment
they do, the customer's action wins.

### 6. "Backup failed — your server is unaffected" is shown for restores, where it is false

`BackupControls.tsx:130-150` is shared between backup and restore. For a restore it renders
*"Restore failed — your server is unaffected · No changes were made to your running server."*
But `BACKUP_RESTORE` is in `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` (`worker/index.ts:50`), and by the time it fails
`worker/restore.ts:103-110` has already stopped the VM and begun overwriting its disk. The most
reassuring message in the product appears in its most destructive failure case.

### 7. `ROADMAP.md` is the file the user reaches for, and it is wrong in both directions

Last updated 2026-07-24 03:50. It marks **"Subscription/billing engine (renewals, grace, suspend,
dunning/termination)"** as `[x]` at line 124 — there is no dunning engine and no card charging. It
simultaneously lists as *unchecked* five things that have shipped (root-password encryption `:61`,
standalone build `:62` — correctly unchecked, non-root web `:64`, SMTP credentials `:80`, 2FA at
login `:84`). The assistant offered at 18:31 to "reconcile ROADMAP.md to reality first so it's
trustworthy" as option (b); the user chose (a) and it was never revisited. The user then asked "what
else needs to be done" five more times.

### 8. Volumes are marketed and modelled as portable; they are not

The whole 17:42–18:05 design discussion concluded on "volumes stay portable — your data survives a
server rebuild and can move between servers," and that framing is in the docs and the UI. In code:

- `lib/actions-volumes.ts:129-131` refuses to attach a volume to any server other than the one
  recorded in `volume.serverId`;
- `worker/volumes.ts:240` never clears `serverId` on detach.

A volume is therefore pinned to its first server for life. Nothing formats or mounts it either — the
attach notification (`worker/volumes.ts:204`) tells the customer to do that themselves, so "one
volume, one filesystem, mounted at a data path" exists only inside the migration engine
(`worker/migrate-real.ts:227`, `:1300`).
